harmfulness.reason: The core advice to 'Water thoroughly' and 'set it in a bucket of water for 20–30 minutes to rewet the core' directly addresses the dehydration and is safe. Going 'up only one pot size' with drainage holes is also sound. Minor concerns: 'Propagate as insurance' invites cutting a plant that just needs water. The trunk check ('cut into it') could wound the plant, though it is conditional on finding mushy tissue. There is also no mention that Dracaena is toxic to cats and dogs.

It ties the diagnosis to case evidence: 'Dry soil that's crowded with roots doesn't absorb water well, so a watering a week ago may not have reached the middle of the root ball.' The core advice (deep soak plus repot into fresh soil) mirrors what the commenters recommended and what worked for the poster. Points off because some details, such as 'brown tips and a few yellowing lower leaves,' are not supported by the case. Some content is also generic, such as the leaf-tip causes, the light and water-quality tips, and 'good time of year' without knowing the season.

feasibility.reason: Every step can be done at home with common items: pressing the stem, soaking in a bucket, repotting one size up into potting mix with perlite, and taking cane cuttings. Steps are numbered and concrete, with sizes and durations given ('1–2 inches wider', '20–30 minutes', '4–6 inches'). The owner could do all of it this week.
